# Semantic and Language Embeddings

Also called: SAM-guided Gaussian Grouping

## Overview
This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting by attaching high-dimensional feature vectors to Gaussian primitives, enabling the real-time rendering of semantic, language, or vision-language embeddings alongside color [S1, S2, unofficial]. It solves the problem of static geometric rendering by distilling 2D vision-model knowledge into a 3D representation, allowing for open-vocabulary segmentation, phrase grounding, and visual question answering via cosine similarity against text embeddings [S1, S2, unofficial]. Unlike sibling methods that focus on appearance or ray tracing, this approach generalizes the alpha-blending accumulation to arbitrary feature spaces [S1, S2, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on the differentiable alpha-blending accumulation of feature vectors during rasterization. For a pixel $p$, the rendered feature vector $\mathbf{F}(p)$ is computed as:

$$
\mathbf{F}(p) = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{O}_p} \mathbf{f}_i \cdot \alpha_i \cdot \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)
$$

where:
*   $\mathcal{O}_p$ is the set of Gaussians overlapping pixel $p$, sorted front-to-back.
*   $\mathbf{f}_i$ is the feature vector (semantic, language, or latent) of Gaussian $i$.
*   $\alpha_i$ is the opacity of Gaussian $i$.
*   The product term represents the transmittance from preceding Gaussians [S1, S2, unofficial].

The resulting 2D feature map is then decoded or compared against text embeddings to enable semantic tasks [S1, S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [3D Gaussian Splatting with Feature Vectors](8060-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-feature-vectors.md)
Attaches a dense feature vector $\mathbf{f}_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$ to each Gaussian, enabling real-time open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by distilling 2D vision-model features (e.g., CLIP) into 3D [8060-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-feature-vectors.md]. It generalizes alpha-blending to arbitrary feature spaces, allowing the 2D feature map to be decoded by segmentation heads or compared against text embeddings via cosine similarity [8060-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-feature-vectors.md]. Choose this for general-purpose open-vocabulary segmentation.

### [Text Embedding Generation with Directional Views](8239-text-embedding-generation-with-directional-views.md)
Generates semantic text embeddings conditioned on specific camera viewpoints to enable view-dependent semantic understanding [8239-text-embedding-generation-with-directional-views.md]. It appends directional view descriptors (e.g., "front", "side") to text prompts before encoding with a frozen CLIP text encoder, allowing the system to distinguish between different perspectives of the same object [8239-text-embedding-generation-with-directional-views.md]. Choose this when semantic meaning varies significantly by viewpoint.

### [LSeg Feature Encoding](12078-lseg-feature-encoding.md)
Attaches semantic feature vectors to 3D Gaussian primitives by distilling knowledge from the 2D LSeg vision-language model [12078-lseg-feature-encoding.md]. It uses multi-scale inference with a ViT-L/16 image encoder and ViT-B/32 text encoder to generate open-vocabulary feature fields for zero-shot segmentation and editing [12078-lseg-feature-encoding.md]. Choose this for high-quality zero-shot segmentation where LSeg's specific training bias (e.g., traffic scenes) is acceptable.

### [VLM-Augmented Segmentation](15758-vlm-augmented-segmentation.md)
Augments 3D Gaussian primitives with compact language features distilled from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) using a scene-specific autoencoder [15758-vlm-augmented-segmentation.md]. It prevents memory explosion by compressing high-dimensional VLM embeddings into a latent space before splatting, then decodes them for alignment with text embeddings [15758-vlm-augmented-segmentation.md]. Choose this for memory-constrained applications requiring VLM-level semantic understanding.

### Language Embedded 3D Gaussians
Expands feature blending to full scene understanding, encoding object-level embeddings for phrase grounding in addition to pixel-level features [S2, unofficial].

### LangSplat
Pioneers open-vocabulary semantic segmentation in real time by rendering feature maps that are compared against text embeddings from CLIP [S2, unofficial].

### 3D Vision-Language GS
Projects vision-language models into the 3DGS framework, training a joint embedding space where rendered feature maps can be queried with natural language [S2, unofficial]. It enables tasks like 3D visual question answering and zero-shot semantic reasoning [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of attaching feature vectors to 3D Gaussians was pioneered by Feature-3DGS and LangSplat, which demonstrated that alpha-blending could render feature maps comparable to CLIP text embeddings for open-vocabulary segmentation [S1, S2, unofficial]. Subsequent work expanded this to object-level phrase grounding (Language Embedded 3D Gaussians) and joint vision-language embedding spaces for visual question answering (3D Vision-Language GS) [S1, S2, unofficial]. The approach is also used for instance grouping supervised by SAM (Segment Anything Model) and video tracking [S1, unofficial].
